osces.title: Brugada Syndrome - Sudden Cardiac Death Risk Stratification

patient.name: Marcus Chen
patient.history_of_presenting_complaint: Presented to ED after losing consciousness while at home with influenza. Wife witnessed brief seizure-like activity lasting 30 seconds. Temperature 39.2°C on arrival. Similar episode 2 years ago during gastroenteritis with fever, dismissed as vasovagal. Father died suddenly at age 42 while sleeping, no autopsy performed. Patient takes no regular medications, non-smoker, occasional alcohol.

physical_examination.general: Alert, mildly unwell with fever, no distress
physical_examination.cardiovascular: Normal S1 S2, no murmurs, no signs of heart failure
physical_examination.neurological: GCS 15, no focal deficits, normal reflexes

ecg.findings: Type 1 Brugada pattern: Coved ST elevation 4mm in V1-V2 with inverted T waves, descending ST segment. Pattern more prominent with fever. Normal QTc 420ms
ecg.interpretation: Diagnostic Type 1 Brugada pattern unmasked by fever

blood_tests.electrolytes: Na 138 mmol/L, K 4.1 mmol/L, Mg 0.92 mmol/L

imaging.chest_xray: Normal cardiac silhouette, clear lung fields
imaging.echocardiogram: Normal LV function EF 60%, normal RV, no structural abnormality

other.24_hour_holter: Brief run of polymorphic VT (8 beats) during sleep
other.ajmaline_provocation_test: Not performed (already spontaneous Type 1 pattern with fever)

avoid_list: Tramadol - Associated with arrhythmias in Brugada

definitive: ICD implantation indicated (syncope + spontaneous Type 1 pattern)
Family screening - ECG + ajmaline provocation for siblings
Avoid fever triggers - immediate paracetamol for any fever
Medical alert bracelet with Brugada diagnosis

expected_outcomes.best_case: ICD successfully prevents sudden cardiac death, family members screened
complications: Inappropriate ICD shocks from supraventricular tachycardia
Psychological impact of sudden death risk
expected_outcomes.prognosis: Good with ICD - 95% survival at 10 years. Without ICD - 10% annual sudden death risk with high-risk features

criteria: Asks about family history of sudden death (1 mark)
Checks temperature and recognises fever (1 mark)
Correctly identifies Type 1 Brugada pattern on ECG (2 marks)
Orders echocardiogram to exclude structural disease (1 mark)
Aggressive fever management with paracetamol (1 mark)
Discusses ICD indication and function (1 mark)
Shows empathy for sudden death risk anxiety (1 mark)

common_pitfalls: Missing Type 1 Brugada pattern on ECG
Delaying ICD referral in high-risk patient
references: CSANZ 2023 Guidelines for Inherited Arrhythmia Syndromes
Heart Rhythm Society 2022 Brugada Syndrome Consensus
eTG Cardiovascular - Sudden Cardiac Death Prevention
Medical Journal of Australia 2023 - Brugada Management

osces.title: Arrhythmogenic Right Ventricular Cardiomyopathy - Young Athlete Sudden Death Prevention

patient.name: Sophie Martinez
patient.history_of_presenting_complaint: Elite netball player experienced sudden palpitations during intense training session yesterday, felt dizzy and had to stop. Teammates noted she looked pale and unsteady. Similar episodes twice in past 6 months during games, attributed to dehydration. No chest pain. Uncle died suddenly at age 28 while jogging, diagnosed with 'heart problem' at autopsy. Patient very concerned about career implications.

physical_examination.cardiovascular: Soft systolic murmur at left sternal edge, normal S1 S2

ecg.findings: Epsilon waves in V1-V3, T wave inversions V1-V4, QRS duration 118ms in V1, premature ventricular complexes with LBBB morphology
ecg.interpretation: Major criteria for ARVC - epsilon waves and T inversions in right precordial leads

blood_tests.electrolytes: Na 139 mmol/L, K 4.3 mmol/L, Mg 0.88 mmol/L

imaging.echocardiogram: RV dilatation PLAX RVOT 38mm, RV regional wall motion abnormalities, RV FAC 28% (reduced), normal LV function
imaging.cardiac_mri: RV ejection fraction 42%, dyskinetic RV free wall, fatty infiltration of RV myocardium, late gadolinium enhancement

other.24_hour_holter: 680 PVCs/24 hours, 2 runs of NSVT (12 beats, 180 bpm)
other.exercise_test: Induced sustained VT at peak exercise (terminated with IV lignocaine)

immediate: Immediate exercise restriction pending full evaluation
Psychology referral for career adjustment support

heart_failure: Consider spironolactone 25mg if progressive RV failure

definitive: ICD implantation (definite ARVC with sustained VT on exercise)
Permanent disqualification from competitive sports (CSANZ guidelines)
Genetic counselling and family cascade screening
Regular surveillance - echo yearly, Holter monitoring
Consider catheter ablation if recurrent VT despite medical therapy

expected_outcomes.best_case: ICD prevents sudden death, accepts career change, family members identified early
complications: Recurrent VT storms requiring multiple ICD shocks
Depression from loss of athletic career
expected_outcomes.prognosis: With ICD and exercise restriction - 85% survival at 10 years. Major predictor is RV function progression

criteria: Explores exercise relationship to symptoms (1 mark)
Identifies family history of sudden death (1 mark)
Quantifies athletic level and training (1 mark)
Identifies epsilon waves on ECG (2 marks)
Orders cardiac MRI for tissue characterisation (1 mark)

common_pitfalls: Delaying ICD in presence of sustained VT
references: 2023 CSANZ Position Statement on Exercise in Genetic Heart Disease
2019 Task Force Criteria for ARVC Diagnosis
Heart Foundation Australia - Sudden Cardiac Death in Athletes
eTG Cardiovascular - Cardiomyopathies

osces.title: Prinzmetal Angina - Calcium Channel Blocker Therapy

patient.name: Robert Thompson
patient.history_of_presenting_complaint: Woken at 3am with severe crushing central chest pain lasting 15 minutes, resolved spontaneously. Four similar episodes over past 2 months, always between 2-5am, never with exertion. Can walk up three flights of stairs without symptoms. Heavy smoker 25 pack-years, drinks 6 standard drinks on weekends. Father had MI at age 65. Takes no regular medications. Recent stress with mine safety investigation.

physical_examination.cardiovascular: Normal heart sounds, no murmurs, no signs heart failure
physical_examination.peripheral: All pulses present, no carotid bruits

ecg.findings: During pain: 3mm ST elevation in inferior leads II, III, aVF. ECG 30 minutes later completely normal
ecg.interpretation: Transient ST elevation consistent with vasospasm

blood_tests.lipids: Total cholesterol 6.2 mmol/L, LDL 3.8 mmol/L, HDL 0.9 mmol/L
blood_tests.electrolytes: Na 140 mmol/L, K 4.2 mmol/L, Mg 0.91 mmol/L

imaging.coronary_angiography: Minimal atherosclerosis, no significant stenosis. Ergonovine provocation induced severe RCA spasm with ST elevation and chest pain, relieved by intracoronary GTN
imaging.echocardiogram: Normal LV function EF 62%, no regional wall motion abnormalities at rest

other.exercise_stress_test: Completed 10 minutes Bruce protocol, no chest pain or ECG changes at peak exercise

immediate: Sublingual GTN spray for acute episodes (PBS: 1696R)

first_line: GTN spray PRN for breakthrough pain (PBS: 1696R)
avoid: Aspirin in high doses - may worsen in some patients

lifestyle: Mandatory smoking cessation - most important intervention
Stress reduction techniques, consider shift work modification

expected_outcomes.best_case: Complete symptom resolution on CCB therapy with smoking cessation
complications: CCB side effects - ankle oedema, constipation
expected_outcomes.prognosis: Excellent if quits smoking and compliant with CCB - 95% angina-free at 1 year. Poor if continues smoking - 40% have MI within 5 years

criteria: Identifies rest pain pattern, especially early morning (1 mark)
Assesses triggers - stress, cold, alcohol (1 mark)
Recognises transient ST elevation pattern (2 marks)
Orders coronary angiography with provocation (1 mark)
Provides GTN for acute episodes (1 mark)

references: eTG Cardiovascular - Variant Angina Management
CSANZ 2023 Guidelines for Chronic Coronary Syndromes
Japanese Circulation Society Guidelines on Vasospastic Angina
Medical Journal of Australia - Prinzmetal Angina Review 2023

osces.title: Atrial Septal Defect - Adult Presentation with Paradoxical Embolism

patient.name: Jennifer Walsh
patient.history_of_presenting_complaint: Developed sudden left arm weakness and speech difficulty during long-haul flight from London. Symptoms lasted 2 hours then completely resolved. Takes combined oral contraceptive pill. Recent diagnosis of 'heart murmur' at routine check but no follow-up. Mild dyspnoea on exertion for years, attributed to fitness. Two pregnancies uncomplicated. Mother has 'hole in heart' diagnosed in childhood, never treated.

physical_examination.cardiovascular: Fixed split S2, grade 2/6 systolic murmur at left upper sternal border, no clubbing
physical_examination.neurological: Full power all limbs, normal reflexes, no residual deficit

ecg.findings: Incomplete RBBB, right axis deviation, peaked P waves in II suggesting right atrial enlargement
ecg.interpretation: Consistent with ASD with right heart volume overload

imaging.transthoracic_echo: Secundum ASD 22mm diameter, left-to-right shunt, dilated RA and RV, estimated Qp:Qs 2.2:1, RVSP 35mmHg
imaging.bubble_study: Positive for right-to-left shunt with Valsalva manoeuvre

other.tee: Large secundum ASD with bidirectional shunt, adequate rims for device closure except inferior rim 4mm
other.cardiac_catheterisation: Qp:Qs ratio 2.3:1, no pulmonary hypertension, suitable for percutaneous closure

immediate: Anticoagulation - apixaban 10mg BD for 7 days then 5mg BD (PBS: 10180R)
definitive: Percutaneous ASD closure with Amplatzer device
follow_up: Bubble echo 6 months post-closure to confirm no residual shunt
Family screening - echo for first-degree relatives

expected_outcomes.best_case: Successful device closure, no further embolic events, improved exercise capacity
expected_outcomes.prognosis: Excellent after closure - stroke risk returns to population baseline. Exercise capacity typically improves within 6 months

criteria: Explores OCP use and flight history (1 mark)
Asks about family history of congenital heart disease (1 mark)
Identifies DVT as embolic source (1 mark)
Arranges TEE for closure planning (1 mark)

common_pitfalls: Missing fixed split S2 on examination
Not identifying OCP as risk factor
references: CSANZ Position Statement on Adult Congenital Heart Disease 2023
eTG Cardiovascular - Atrial Septal Defects
European Society of Cardiology Guidelines on Adult CHD 2020
Stroke Foundation Australia - Cryptogenic Stroke Guidelines

osces.title: Cardiorenal Syndrome - Managing Heart Failure with Renal Dysfunction

patient.name: George Papadopoulos
patient.presenting_complaint: Worsening shortness of breath and leg swelling
patient.history_of_presenting_complaint: Admitted with NYHA III heart failure symptoms, orthopnoea (4 pillows), PND, bilateral leg oedema to mid-thigh. Weight gain 8kg over 2 weeks. Background of ischaemic cardiomyopathy (STEMI 2019), CKD stage 3b (baseline creatinine 160 μmol/L), type 2 diabetes, hypertension. Current medications include furosemide 40mg BD, perindopril 5mg, bisoprolol 5mg, spironolactone 25mg. Creatinine on admission 180 μmol/L, now 250 μmol/L after 3 days IV furosemide.

physical_examination.general: Dyspnoeic at rest, using accessory muscles
physical_examination.cardiovascular: JVP 10cm, displaced apex beat, S3 gallop, bilateral pitting oedema to sacrum

blood_tests.renal_function: Creatinine 250 μmol/L (baseline 160), eGFR 22 mL/min/1.73m², Urea 18 mmol/L

imaging.chest_xray: Cardiomegaly, pulmonary congestion, bilateral pleural effusions
imaging.echocardiogram: LV EF 28%, global hypokinesis, moderate MR, moderate TR, RVSP 55mmHg, dilated IVC no collapse

immediate: Continue IV furosemide 80mg BD despite creatinine rise

diuretic_strategy.rationale: Creatinine rise acceptable if decongesting - improved outcomes
additions: Add metolazone 2.5mg daily if inadequate response (sequential nephron blockade)
Consider furosemide infusion 10mg/hr if bolus ineffective
monitoring: Continue despite creatinine rise if JVP decreasing

add: Empagliflozin 10mg daily (PBS: 11748Q) - cardiorenal protection even with low eGFR
Iron carboxymaltose 1000mg IV for iron deficiency (ferritin <100)
avoid: Metformin - lactic acidosis risk with eGFR <30

advanced_options: Right heart catheterisation to guide therapy
Consider cardiac resynchronisation therapy if LBBB
Evaluate for heart transplant/LVAD if refractory

expected_outcomes.best_case: Successful decongestion, creatinine improves to 180-200 μmol/L, symptoms resolve, discharge on oral therapy
expected_outcomes.acceptable: Creatinine settles at 220-250 μmol/L but patient decongested and symptom-free
expected_outcomes.prognosis: Type 2 cardiorenal syndrome - 30% 1-year mortality. SGLT2i reduces hospitalisation by 25%

criteria: Continues diuresis despite creatinine rise (2 marks)
Maintains ACE inhibitor if possible (1 mark)

common_pitfalls: Stopping diuretics due to rising creatinine (worsens outcomes)
Not recognising SGLT2i benefit in HFrEF with CKD
Missing iron deficiency in heart failure
references: CSANZ 2024 Heart Failure Guidelines Update
KDIGO Guidelines on Cardiorenal Syndrome
eTG Cardiovascular - Acute Decompensated Heart Failure
SGLT2 inhibitors in Heart Failure - EMPEROR-Reduced Trial
